rows.description: I tell my friend "your drawing is so good". I feel happy giving kind words and want to learn how they did it. Admiring without envy is a lovely early skill, and asking "will you show me?" is a wise next step.

related mind states: joy, affection, admiration, envy

rows.description: I am so angry about no sweets that I scream and throw myself down. My body feels too big to control. A wise grown-up stays calm, keeps the limit and helps me breathe. The immature pattern is hitting or throwing things.
graph_context: same situation, other stances at this age: fear, shame
paired view exists: Receiver (S501)
related mind states: anger, calm, relief from stress

rows.description: My parent stays calm and says "I know you are upset, the answer is still no". I feel safe because the limit does not break. Firm love teaches that big feelings pass and rules are steady.
graph_context: same situation, other stances at this age: anger, fear, shame
related mind states: affection, calm, trust

rows.description: My parent shouts and threatens when I have a tantrum. I feel frightened and stop crying but I am not learning. It is not my fault that feelings are big. A calmer repair afterwards, with a hug and an explanation, helps.
graph_context: same situation, other stances at this age: fear, shame
paired view exists: Actor (S499)
related mind states: affection, sadness, anger, fear

rows.description: After the tantrum in the market I feel embarrassed and sorry, and I hide my face. A wise parent says "you were upset, it is over, let us fix it". Calling me bad makes the shame stay stuck.
graph_context: same situation, other stances at this age: anger, fear
related mind states: shame, embarrassment

rows.description: I learn to hug my teddy, blow "birthday candle" breaths and say "I am angry". I feel proud when I calm down. Naming a feeling and doing a small calming action are the early steps to self-control.
graph_context: same situation, other stances at this age: anger, fear, shame
related mind states: affection, anger, pride, calm

rows.description: A friend has a huge tantrum at school and I feel scared and unsure. Wise action: step back, tell a teacher and be kind later. Their feelings are big, not dangerous, and I am not responsible for fixing them.
graph_context: same situation, other stances at this age: anger, shame
related mind states: affection, anger, fear

rows.description: My parent said no to the toy and I am furious, I feel like they do not love me right now. A wise child asks "can I have it on my birthday?" The immature pattern is crying and screaming until the parent gives in.
graph_context: same situation, other stances at this age: manipulation, resentment, trust
related mind states: affection, sadness, anger

rows.description: I ask for one more show and hear no. I grumble but I believe my parent has a good reason. Trust grows when the no is kind and consistent, and I begin to accept rules without a fight.
graph_context: same situation, other stances at this age: anger, manipulation, resentment
related mind states: trust

rows.description: I say "you are mean, I hate you" and feel both angry and afraid to have said it. Wise reply from a parent: "you are angry, I still love you". Children need to learn hard words do not end love.
graph_context: same situation, other stances at this age: anger, manipulation, trust
